ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Megan Quigley.

From helping people navigate benefits
to asking how systems could serve them better.

≠

Where this question started.

In my work on financial wellness at Lincoln Financial and in human resources at NBCUniversal, I saw people miss support because they did not know it existed, were unsure whether they qualified, or struggled with timing, enrollment, and follow-through.

Available ≠ Accessible grows from those observations. I wanted to understand what happens between a policy’s promise and a person’s experience—and how implementation could make the path easier.

My experience motivates the question. The findings come from the public research cited throughout this project.

ABOUT THIS PROJECT

Why this project exists.

I created Available ≠ Accessible to explore a question that has stayed with me: what does it take to turn an available benefit into support someone can actually use?

I use public research and visual stories to make the steps, barriers, and gaps easier to see. My goal is to help readers understand how these programs work and connect with resources that may be useful to them.

This is my independent project, based on published evidence. I am not affiliated with the programs discussed.
